name: Multi-envelope oscillator-level morphing pad
goal: Create an always-in-motion pad by silencing shared amp control of oscillators and assigning staggered envelope-mode LFOs to each oscillator level (plus optional noise), with differing filter and WT motion.

source.title: This One Technique Changes EVERYTHING // Vital Pad Sound Design Tutorial

prerequisites: Synth with ≥3 osc, multiple loopable envelopes or envelope-mode LFOs, filters, noise/sample osc

inputs.name: release_seconds
inputs.description: Long shared release so notes trail (tutorial ~5s on env1)

outputs.name: morphing_pad_patch
outputs.description: Pad whose layers enter/exit on independent timings

constraints: Ground every step in the source YouTube-provided captions; do not invent UI or settings.
Original synthesis only — map brand UI (Serum/Vital/Pigments/Phase Plant/etc.) to portable osc/filter/FX roles for a browser or generic hybrid synth; never rip presets, wavetables, or samples.
Prefer transferable signal-flow and motion relationships over vendor-specific preset names.
Methodology is synth-agnostic: any instrument with per-osc level envelopes (or envelope-mode LFOs) works.
Do not depend on a specific commercial wavetable pack; use stock or original tables.

steps.action: Lengthen the main amp release (~5s) so held chords trail instead of cutting off.
Enable all target oscillators but set their levels to zero.
Convert LFO1/2/3 (or dedicated envelopes) to envelope mode; draw distinct ADSR-like shapes with different attack times; route each to one oscillator’s level.
Optionally octave-shift and pan layers so the staggered entries are obvious while designing.
Assign different filters (e.g. one ladder vs another) to subsets of oscillators; reduce resonance; let early layers swoop while a late layer arrives darker/brighter.
steps.expect: Layers feel like separate parts of one patch

steps.action: Add noise/sample with its own short attack–release envelope to level; optionally direct-out before main FX for drama.
steps.expect: Timed noise wash independent of tonal oscs

steps.action: Animate wavetable position with synced LFOs; add mild unison/spread on select oscs; optional random bipolar pan.
Finish with long ambient delay/reverb (tutorial example: long room ~tens of seconds decay) on a send or insert.
steps.expect: Motion remains audible inside a wash

verification: Not all oscillators share one identical amp envelope timing
At least two distinct entry times audible on a held chord
Noise or WT motion optional but level-stagger is present
